title: Long-term follow-up for bimanual microincision cataract surgery: comparison of results obtained by surgeons in training and experienced surgeons

indication: Age-related cataract LOCS III grade 2-3; previous surgery, complicated cataract, uveitis, glaucoma, corneal opacity, mydriasis below 4 mm, ECD below 1500 cells/mm2 and one-eyed patients excluded; some patients contributed both eyes

groups.description: Group A: bimanual microincision cataract surgery (B-MICS, Stellaris, Akreos MI60 IOL) by three surgeons in training on their first B-MICS cases under expert supervision; 80 eyes of 62 patients; tobramycin/dexamethasone then flurbiprofen
Group B: the same B-MICS technique by three experienced surgeons (the article's comparison group); 80 eyes of 59 patients; same postoperative regimen

series.baseline_label: Preoperative corneal pachymetry of the operated eye (Table 1 column 'Preoperative'); IOPac pachymeter, Heidelberg Engineering (Methods)
series.notes: Table 1 (Group A) row 'Corneal pachymetry (µm)', columns Preoperative, 1 month, 18 months; footnote: mean ± standard deviation. Methods state the first postoperative visit as 30 days; the table label '1 month' is used. All Group A surgeries had an 18-month follow-up (Methods); per-visit n not tabulated.

series.baseline_label: Preoperative corneal pachymetry of the operated eye (Table 2 column 'Preoperative'); IOPac pachymeter, Heidelberg Engineering (Methods)
series.notes: Table 2 (Group B) row 'Corneal pachymetry (µm)', columns Preoperative, 1 month, 18 months; footnote: mean ± standard deviation. Methods state the first postoperative visit as 30 days; the table label '1 month' is used. Per-visit n not tabulated.

exclusions.what: Tables 1 and 2 BCVA, astigmatism and endothelial count rows
Mean pachymetry increase at 18 months (Results text)
exclusions.reason: Text values of a change; the tabulated absolute series are used

exclusions.what: Tables 4-6 incision length/angle and morphology (AS-OCT of the clear corneal incisions), including the iris-prolapse subgroups of Group A
exclusions.reason: Incision architecture, not central corneal thickness; subgroups defined by an intraoperative event

notes: The groups differ by surgeon experience with the same standard technique, not by an investigational agent, device or technique variant: both are control-role, separate groups (same decision as the endothelium record ecd-pmc4888734).

Method: the article names the pachymeter (IOPac; Heidelberg Engineering) without its principle; the IOPac is a handheld ultrasound pachymeter, so method = ultrasound. The tables label the row 'Corneal pachymetry' and the measurement location is not stated; it is taken as central corneal thickness (standard for this handheld pachymetry), which is an extraction assumption.
Patients with ocular pathology during follow-up not related to surgery were excluded from the cohort (Methods); two Group A IOLs were placed in the sulcus after intraoperative complications.
